title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
statement:
A **trie** (prefix tree) stores a set of words so that words and prefixes can be looked up in time proportional to their length. Typical uses are a dictionary or searching a phone's contact list as you type.

Implement a trie that supports three operations on lowercase words:

- `insert w`: add the word `w` to the set (inserting a word that is already present changes nothing). Prints nothing.
- `search w`: print `true` if exactly the word `w` was inserted earlier, otherwise `false`. A word that is only a prefix of an inserted word does not count.
- `startsWith p`: print `true` if at least one inserted word begins with the prefix `p` (a word is a prefix of itself), otherwise `false`.

Process the operations in order and print one line for every `search` and `startsWith` operation.

**Follow-up:** explain why each trie node needs an end-of-word flag. For example, after inserting only `car`, `startsWith ca` must be `true` while `search ca` must be `false`; without the flag the two cases cannot be told apart. Also discuss why a trie is a good fit for storing a dictionary or contacts compared with a hash set of words.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `q`, the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines contains an operation name (`insert`, `search` or `startsWith`) and a word, separated by a space.
outputFormat: For every `search` and `startsWith` operation print `true` or `false` on its own line, in order.
constraints: The total length of all words in the input is at most 3 · 10^5

examples.input:
7
insert car
search car
search ca
startsWith ca
insert ca
search ca
startsWith cat
examples.explanation: `car` was inserted, so `search car` is true. `ca` is only a prefix of it, so `search ca` is false while `startsWith ca` is true. After `insert ca` the word `ca` is stored, so `search ca` becomes true. No word starts with `cat`.

examples.input:
6
insert zoe
insert zoo
startsWith zo
startsWith z
search zo
startsWith zoom
examples.explanation: Both stored words start with `zo` and with `z`. `zo` itself was never inserted, and no stored word begins with `zoom`, so both of those answers are false.

complexity.time: O(L) per operation, where L is the length of the word

hints: Each node represents one prefix and has up to 26 children, one for each next letter. The root represents the empty prefix.
To insert, walk down creating missing children, then mark the final node as the end of a word. To look something up, walk down and stop with false if a child is missing.
`search` and `startsWith` walk the same path. They differ only in the last check: `search` also requires the end-of-word mark on the node it reaches.
